questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut is used to quickly save a workbook in MS-Excel 365?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + S**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ctrl + S** is the universal keyboard shortcut to save a workbook or document in MS-Excel 365 as well as other Microsoft Office applications.
 
• Using this shortcut ensures that the current state of your workbook is saved to the disk, preventing data loss during unexpected events like software crashes.
 
• The shortcut works across all versions of Microsoft Excel, including MS-Excel 365, Excel 2019, and earlier versions.
 
• Users can simply press **Ctrl + S** on Windows or **Command + S** on macOS to save their work quickly.
 
• In addition to saving manually, Excel 365 also offers an AutoSave feature when files are stored on OneDrive or SharePoint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in MS-Excel:** Excel provides various shortcuts for efficient workflow, such as **Ctrl + C** for copy, **Ctrl + V** for paste, and **Ctrl + P** for printing.
 
• **AutoSave Feature:** Excel 365 automatically saves files to OneDrive or SharePoint in real-time, provided the feature is enabled, reducing dependency on manual saving.
 
• **File Formats:** MS-Excel saves workbooks in formats like **.xlsx** (default), **.xls** (older format), and **.csv** (for data exchange). Users can select formats while saving.
 
• **Save As Functionality:** The *Save As* option allows users to save a copy of their workbook under a different name or location, accessible through the shortcut **F12**.
 
• **Cloud Integration:** MS-Excel 365 is integrated with Microsoft OneDrive, enabling collaborative editing, version history, and secure cloud storage.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the taskbar in the Windows desktop interface?

options.text: It stores documents and media files.
It provides access to open and frequently used programs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides access to open and frequently used programs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The taskbar is a primary feature of the Windows desktop interface that provides quick access to open programs and frequently used applications.
 
• It contains the "Start" button, which opens the Start Menu, allowing users to search for and launch installed programs.
 
• Users can pin their favorite applications to the taskbar for easy access, reducing the need to navigate through directories.
 
• The taskbar also displays active programs, enabling users to switch between them using simple clicks.
 
• Additional features include the system tray, where users can view notifications and access background-running programs like antivirus software, Wi-Fi, and volume controls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taskbar Terminology:** The taskbar consists of key components such as the Start button, pinned apps, active program icons, and the system tray.
 
• **Customizability:** Users can customize the taskbar by resizing it, changing its position (top, bottom, left, or right of the screen), and choosing which icons are displayed.
 
• **Multi-Monitor Support:** In Windows 10 and later versions, the taskbar can be extended across multiple monitors, providing flexibility for users working on multi-screen setups.
 
• **Search Bar Integration:** The taskbar often integrates with a search bar, enabling users to perform quick searches for files, settings, or web content directly from the desktop.
 
• **Evolution Over Time:** The taskbar has evolved significantly since its introduction in Windows 95, incorporating features like Cortana, virtual desktops, and app previews in newer versions of Windows.

questions.question: Which of the following is true when you delete a file and it is placed in the Recycle Bin on Windows?

options.text: The file is permanently removed from the system and cannot be restored.
The file is moved to the system's storage space but remains inaccessible until permanently deleted.
The file remains locked and cannot be accessed or deleted further.
The file can be restored by right-clicking it and selecting the 'Restore' option.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The file can be restored by right-clicking it and selecting the 'Restore' option.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a file is deleted in Windows, it is typically moved to the Recycle Bin instead of being permanently erased from the system.
 
• The Recycle Bin acts as a temporary storage area for deleted files, allowing users to restore them if needed.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin can be restored by right-clicking on the file and selecting the 'Restore' option, which returns the file to its original location.
 
• Until permanently deleted, files in the Recycle Bin continue to occupy storage space on the system.
 
• The Recycle Bin serves as a safeguard against accidental file deletions, offering users the ability to recover files easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin:** A feature in Windows operating systems designed to temporarily store deleted files and folders until they are permanently removed.
 
• **Permanently Deleting Files:** Files can be permanently removed from the system by emptying the Recycle Bin or using the "Shift + Delete" command.
 
• **Storage Space:** The Recycle Bin occupies a portion of the hard disk space, which can be configured by the user based on their storage requirements.
 
• **Restoration Process:** Restoring files from the Recycle Bin reverts them to their original location on the system, ensuring minimal data loss.
 
• **File Locking:** Files in the Recycle Bin are not locked and can be permanently deleted or restored at any time by the user.

questions.question: In MS Word 365, which feature allows users to customise the appearance of bulleted lists by selecting different bullet styles or symbols and modifying their size and color?
questions.solution:

__

• Users can modify the **size, color, and alignment** of bullets using the Bullet Library feature to match document requirements.
 
• The feature is accessible via the **“Home” tab** under the “Paragraph” group, where the bullet dropdown menu is located.
 
• It offers predefined bullet styles and allows users to define their own using the **“Define New Bullet”** option.
 
• The Bullet Library enhances the visual appeal and readability of documents by enabling personalized list formatting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bulleted vs. Numbered Lists:**

 
 
• Bulleted lists are used for unordered items, while numbered lists are used for sequences or prioritization.
 
• MS Word provides separate tools for managing both types of lists under the “Paragraph” group.
 
 
 
• **Define New Bullet:**
 
 
• This option allows users to create custom bullets using symbols, pictures, or fonts like Wingdings.

• **Paragraph Formatting:**
 
 
• In addition to bullets, users can adjust line spacing, indentation, and alignment to enhance list presentation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about RAM and ROM with reference to computer memory is correct?

options.text: RAM cannot be written to, only read from.
RAM temporarily stores data for active programs, while ROM permanently stores firmware.
RAM is non-volatile, while ROM is volatile.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM temporarily stores data for active programs, while ROM permanently stores firmware**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data for active programs and processes.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a non-volatile memory that permanently stores firmware or essential instructions required for booting up the system.
 
• RAM is faster than ROM because it is designed to handle data at high speeds for real-time operations.
 
• Unlike RAM, which loses its data when the system is powered off, ROM retains its data even without power.
 
• ROM is primarily used for storage of critical instructions (e.g., BIOS), while RAM is used for dynamic data processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile vs Non-Volatile Memory:** Volatile memory (e.g., RAM) requires constant power to retain data, while non-volatile memory (e.g., ROM) retains data even when power is lost.
 
• **Firmware:** Firmware refers to the permanent software programmed into ROM that provides low-level control for a device's hardware.
 
• **RAM Types:** Common types of RAM include DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM). DRAM is slower and cheaper, while SRAM is faster and more expensive.
 
• **ROM Variants:** ROM comes in various types such as PROM (Programmable ROM), EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM), and EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM).
 
• **Importance of RAM:** Higher RAM capacity allows for better multitasking and faster processing of applications, making it a critical component for system performance.

questions.question: In MS Word 2019, if you want to select an entire paragraph quickly, which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Right-click and choose 'Paragraph' from the available menu options.
Press and hold Alt while clicking the paragraph.
Triple-click on any word within the paragraph.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Triple-click on any word within the paragraph**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **MS Word 2019**, selecting an entire paragraph quickly can save time and effort during editing tasks.
 
• **Triple-clicking on any word** within the paragraph is the fastest method to select the entire paragraph. This action highlights the entire block of text immediately.
 
• This functionality works in most modern versions of **Microsoft Word**, including the **2019 edition**.
 
• The reason why triple-clicking works is that Word recognizes text structures like words, sentences, and paragraphs. Triple-clicking is a shortcut for paragraph selection.
 
• Using this shortcut eliminates the need to drag the cursor manually, which can be prone to errors, especially with large paragraphs or precise selections.
 
• This feature is part of Word's user-friendly design, ensuring efficiency in text formatting and editing.
 
• It is particularly useful in situations involving **multi-paragraph documents**, such as reports, essays, or official letters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right-click and choose 'Paragraph'**__

 __
 
• The **right-click** menu provides options for formatting and paragraph settings like alignment, spacing, and indentation, but it does not select the entire paragraph.
 
• This option is more suitable for **customizing paragraph layout** rather than for selection.
 
 
 
• **Press and hold Alt while clicking the paragraph**__
 __
 
• Pressing and holding **Alt** is used for rectangular selection or selecting specific areas of text, not for selecting an entire paragraph.
 
• This feature is helpful in creating columnar or block text selections.
 
 
 
• **Double-click anywhere in the paragraph**__
 
 
• **Double-clicking** selects a single word, not the entire paragraph.
 
• It is a useful shortcut when you want to edit or format a specific word quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes the function of the 'Spill Range' feature introduced in newer versions of MS Excel?

options.text: . It allows multiple users to simultaneously edit different ranges within the same worksheet
It restricts data entry within a specific range of cells based on predefined criteria
It dynamically resizes a formula's output range when the formula returns multiple values.
It automatically saves the workbook to a cloud location at predefined intervals.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It dynamically resizes a formula's output range when the formula returns multiple values.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Spill Range** feature is part of the **dynamic array functionality** introduced in **newer versions of MS Excel**, such as Excel 365 and Excel 2019.
 
• When a formula returns multiple values, the output automatically "spills" into adjacent cells, creating a dynamic range.
 
• This eliminates the need for manually copying formulas into multiple cells, enhancing **efficiency**.
 
• The spill range is automatically updated when the formula is changed or when new data is added, ensuring a **dynamic and responsive data structure**.
 
• Common functions like **SEQUENCE, SORT, FILTER, UNIQUE, RANDARRAY** utilize spill ranges to dynamically display multiple outputs.
 
• If adjacent cells already contain data preventing the "spill," Excel will display a **#SPILL! error**, signaling a conflict in the output range.
 
• This feature is particularly useful for handling **arrays** and performing complex data manipulations with ease.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: It allows multiple users to simultaneously edit different ranges within the same worksheet**__

 __
 
• This feature is unrelated to the **Spill Range functionality**. Collaborative editing in Excel is supported through **Excel Online** or real-time co-authoring features in cloud-based versions.
 
• It enables teams to work together on the same file, but does not dynamically handle formula outputs.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It restricts data entry within a specific range of cells based on predefined criteria**__
 __
 
• This refers to **Data Validation**, a tool used to limit or control the type of data entered into cells.
 
• Data validation is useful for ensuring accuracy and consistency but does not involve dynamic resizing or formula outputs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It automatically saves the workbook to a cloud location at predefined intervals**__
 
 
• This describes the **AutoSave feature** available in Microsoft Office applications integrated with **OneDrive or SharePoint**.
 
• AutoSave ensures that your work is saved continuously to avoid data loss, but it does not relate to the handling of dynamic formula outputs.

questions.question: Which element of the MS Excel interface displays the name of the currently active cell or the selected range of cells?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Name Box**__

__
 
• The **Name Box** is an essential element of the MS Excel interface.
 
• It is located near the **top-left corner** of the Excel window, just above the spreadsheet grid.
 
• The Name Box displays the **name or reference** of the currently active cell (e.g., A1, B2) or the selected range of cells.
 
• Users can use the Name Box to **navigate directly to a specific cell** by entering the cell reference and pressing Enter.
 
• It also allows users to **assign names to ranges**, making data management and formula creation easier.
 
• The Name Box helps in identifying the active cell quickly, which is essential for performing operations like entering data or writing formulas.
 
• This feature is particularly useful in large datasets where navigating and identifying specific cells might be challenging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Status Bar**__

 __
 
• The **Status Bar** is located at the bottom of the Excel window.
 
• It provides information about **current actions**, such as the sum, average, or count of selected cells.
 
• It does not display the name of the active cell; instead, it shows status messages and quick calculations.
 
 
 
• **The Ribbon**__
 __
 
• The Ribbon is the **menu interface** located at the top of Excel.
 
• It contains tabs like **Home, Insert, Page Layout, Formulas, etc.**, which house various tools and commands.
 
• The Ribbon is used for performing tasks like formatting, chart creation, and applying formulas, but it doesn’t display cell references.
 
 
 
• **The Formula Bar**__
 
 
• The Formula Bar is located directly below the Ribbon.
 
• It displays the **contents of the active cell**, including formulas and data.
 
• While it shows the data in the cell, it does not display the cell reference like the Name Box does.

questions.question: What happens when you press Ctrl + S while working on a document in computer system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saves the current document**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Ctrl + S** in most computer applications is the universal shortcut for saving the current document or file.
 
• This shortcut command is commonly used in software like **Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other text or file editors**.
 
• It ensures that any changes made to the document are stored in the permanent memory (like the hard drive) to avoid data loss.
 
• If the document has not been saved previously, the system will prompt the user to **choose a file name and location** for saving.
 
• Regularly saving your work using **Ctrl + S** is a good practice to prevent loss of data due to unexpected crashes or errors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:**

 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are combinations of keys that provide quick access to common functions in applications.
 
• For example, **Ctrl + C** is used to copy, **Ctrl + V** to paste, and **Ctrl + Z** to undo the last action.
 
• These shortcuts help improve productivity and reduce reliance on mouse clicks.
 
 
 
• **Save vs Save As:**
 
 
• The **Save** command updates the current file with any changes made, while **Save As** allows saving the file under a new name or in a different location.
 
• Save As is particularly useful when creating multiple versions of a document.
 
 
 
• **AutoSave Feature:**
 
 
• Many modern applications include an AutoSave feature that periodically saves the document in the background.
 
• This feature minimizes data loss in case of system crashes or power outages.
 
• For example, Microsoft Office applications have AutoSave enabled for files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint.
 
 
 
• **File Formats:**
 
 
• When saving a document, users can choose from various file formats such as **.docx, .pdf, .txt, or .xls**, depending on the software.
 
• Each format serves a specific purpose—for instance, **.pdf** is often used for read-only sharing, while **.docx** is editable.

questions.question: Which version of Windows introduced the Start menu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows 95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows 95** was the first version of the Windows operating system to introduce the Start menu, a revolutionary feature for navigation.
 
• The Start menu combined the list of installed programs with quick access to system settings, making it user-friendly and efficient.
 
• It was launched on **August 24, 1995**, and marked a significant shift towards graphical user interfaces (GUI).
 
• The Start button, located at the bottom-left corner of the screen, became a hallmark of Windows operating systems.
 
• This version also introduced other innovations like the taskbar, long file names, and built-in support for plug-and-play hardware.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Windows Operating System:**

 
 
• Windows is a family of operating systems developed by Microsoft, designed for personal computers, tablets, and embedded systems.
 
• It is one of the most widely used operating systems globally, with billions of active installations.
 
 
 
• **Graphical User Interface (GUI):**
 
 
• The GUI allows users to interact with electronic devices through visual indicators like icons and buttons instead of text-based interfaces.
 
• Windows 95 was a major step forward in popularizing GUI for mainstream computer users.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The taskbar, introduced in Windows 95, allows users to see and switch between open applications easily.
 
• It is located at the bottom of the screen and includes the Start button, quick launch icons, and the system clock.
 
 
 
• **Plug and Play (PnP):**
 
 
• Windows 95 introduced built-in support for PnP, allowing hardware devices to be automatically recognized and configured by the operating system.
 
• This feature greatly simplified the process of adding new hardware to a computer.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Start Menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu became an iconic feature of Windows, evolving through subsequent versions like Windows XP, Windows 7, and Windows 10.
 
• It remains a central element for accessing applications and settings in modern Windows systems.

questions.question: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Press Shift + Delete**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Shift + Delete** bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes a file from the system.
 
• This action removes the file from the file system table, making it inaccessible to the user unless recovery methods are employed.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Windows OS that stores deleted files temporarily until manually cleared.
 
• Files deleted using **Shift + Delete** cannot be restored through the Recycle Bin.
 
• For accidental permanent deletion, specialized data recovery software may be required to retrieve the file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin in Windows OS**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a special folder where deleted files are temporarily stored.
 
• Users can restore files from the Recycle Bin unless the bin has been emptied or files are deleted permanently using Shift + Delete.
 
• The Recycle Bin can be customized to allocate a specific amount of storage space for deleted files.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Deletion**
 
 
• Permanent deletion bypasses temporary storage locations like the Recycle Bin.
 
• It removes file references from the file system, but the actual data remains on the storage device until overwritten.
 
• Tools like disk shredders can be used to overwrite deleted files, ensuring complete erasure.
 
 
 
• **Data Recovery**
 
 
• Data recovery tools like EaseUS or Recuva can retrieve files that have been deleted permanently, provided the data has not been overwritten.
 
• Recovery is more successful if attempted promptly after deletion.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Windows**
 
 
• Shift + Delete: Permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
 
• Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V: Copy and paste files or content.
 
• Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.
 
• Ctrl + Z: Undo the last action.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the .ppsx file format in MS PowerPoint 365?

options.text: To save the presentation in a format that opens directly in Slide Show mode
To save the presentation in a read-only format
To save the presentation as a template for future use
To compress the presentation file size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To save the presentation in a format that opens directly in Slide Show mode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The .ppsx file format in MS PowerPoint is specifically designed to open presentations directly in **Slide Show mode**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the role of RAM and ROM in a computer system?

options.text: RAM is used to store the operating system and permanent files, while ROM is used to store temporary data.
ROM is used for storing data that can be modified and written to, while RAM stores fixed data.
ROM is used to store system firmware, while RAM stores temporary data for active processes.
RAM is non-volatile, while ROM is volatile

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM is used to store system firmware, while RAM stores temporary data for active processes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a non-volatile memory that stores firmware, which includes the BIOS or UEFI needed for starting the computer system.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory used to store temporary data required by active processes and running applications.
 
• Data in RAM is lost when the computer is powered off, whereas data in ROM remains intact irrespective of power status.
 
• ROM provides essential instructions for booting up the computer, while RAM enables multitasking and smooth execution of programs.
 
• Examples of ROM include EEPROM, PROM, and flash memory, while RAM is often categorized as DRAM or SRAM.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory):**

 
 
• It is non-volatile, meaning it retains data even when the power is turned off.
 
• ROM is mainly used for storing system firmware and permanent instructions required during the startup process.
 
• Examples include the BIOS/UEFI in computers and firmware in embedded systems.
 
 
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• It is volatile, meaning data is lost when the power is turned off.
 
• RAM allows quick read/write operations and is used for temporary data storage during the execution of tasks.
 
• Types of RAM include DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM).
 
 
 
• **Firmware:**
 
 
• Firmware is a type of software embedded in hardware devices, stored in ROM.
 
• It provides low-level control and functionality to hardware components.
 
 
 
• **Volatile vs Non-Volatile Memory:**
 
 
• Volatile memory (e.g., RAM) requires power to maintain stored data.
 
• Non-volatile memory (e.g., ROM) retains data even after the power is turned off.

questions.question: Which of the following devices can function as both input and output devices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Touch Screen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **touch screen** is an electronic display that can act as both an **input and output device**.
 
• As an input device, it allows users to interact with the system by touching the screen using a finger or stylus.
 
• As an output device, it displays visual content, such as text, images, or videos, similar to a regular screen or monitor.
 
• Touch screens are commonly used in smartphones, tablets, ATMs, interactive kiosks, and other digital devices.
 
• They employ various technologies such as resistive, capacitive, infrared, or surface acoustic wave to detect and process touch inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistive Touch Screen:**

 
 
• It uses two electrically conductive layers separated by a small gap.
 
• When pressure is applied to the screen, the layers come into contact, registering the touch input.
 
• Commonly used in older devices and ATM machines.
 
 
 
• **Capacitive Touch Screen:**
 
 
• It works by sensing the electrical conductivity of the user's finger.
 
• Capacitive screens are more responsive and support multi-touch gestures.
 
• They are widely used in smartphones and modern tablets.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Touch Screen:**
 
 
• This technology uses infrared light beams to detect touch.
 
• It does not require physical contact; even proximity can register input.
 
• Typically found in interactive kiosks and large touch displays.
 
 
 
• **Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) Touch Screen:**
 
 
• SAW screens rely on ultrasonic waves that pass over the touch screen surface.
 
• When the screen is touched, the waves are absorbed, allowing the location of the touch to be determined.
 
• They provide high clarity and durability but are sensitive to external contaminants.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Touch Screens:**
 
 
• Touch screens are widely used in **retail stores, healthcare, education, gaming, and industrial automation.**
 
• They enable intuitive user experiences, reducing the need for external peripherals like keyboards or mice.

questions.question: In the context of computer memory hierarchy, which of the following statements regarding access speed and cost per bit is generally true as you move from registers towards secondary storage?

options.text: Access speed increases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed increases and cost per bit increases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit increases.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As we move down the memory hierarchy—from registers to secondary storage—the **access speed decreases**. Registers are the fastest, while secondary storage devices like hard drives are significantly slower.
 
• The **cost per bit of storage decreases** as we move from registers to secondary storage. Registers and cache are expensive due to their high-speed performance and small size.
 
• Registers are located within the CPU, offering **nanosecond-level access times**, whereas secondary storage devices like HDDs or SSDs have access times in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
• Secondary storage devices, such as hard drives, offer **much larger storage capacity** at a lower cost per bit but are slower in terms of data retrieval compared to primary memory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Memory Hierarchy in Computers**

 
 
• It refers to the arrangement of memory types based on **speed, cost, and capacity**.
 
• It typically includes registers, cache, main memory (RAM), and secondary storage (HDD/SSD).
 
• Registers and cache are the fastest but have the smallest capacity, while secondary storage is slower but offers large capacity.
 
 
 
• **Access Time**
 
 
• Access time is the time taken by the CPU to retrieve data from memory.
 
• Registers have the shortest access time, measured in nanoseconds, while secondary storage access time is measured in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
 
 
• **Cost per Bit**
 
 
• Cost per bit refers to the expense incurred for storing one bit of data.
 
• Registers and cache have the highest cost per bit, while secondary storage devices have the lowest cost per bit.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Storage**
 
 
• Includes devices like HDDs, SSDs, and optical disks.
 
• It is non-volatile and provides persistent storage for data even when the system is powered off.
 
 
 
• **Registers**
 
 
• Smallest and fastest memory located directly within the CPU.
 
• Used to temporarily store data that is actively being processed by the CPU.

questions.question: Consider a computer system with a multi-core processor. What is the primary advantage of having multiple cores compared to a single-core processor with the same clock speed when executing multiple independent tasks simultaneously?

Improved ability to handle and execute multiple separate processes concurrently

__
 
• Multi-core processors allow multiple cores to work independently, enabling efficient execution of multiple independent tasks simultaneously.
 
• This architecture reduces bottlenecks caused by task switching in single-core systems, improving overall system performance.
 
• Each core operates as a separate processing unit, facilitating better multitasking and parallel processing capabilities.
 
• Multi-core systems are especially advantageous in environments requiring concurrent execution of multiple processes, such as servers or multimedia applications.
 
• While clock speed remains the same, multiple cores ensure more tasks are processed in parallel, leading to better utilization of system resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core:** A core is a processing unit within a CPU that performs computational tasks. Multi-core CPUs contain multiple cores in a single chip.
 
• **Parallel Processing:** The simultaneous execution of multiple processes or tasks by dividing them across multiple cores to improve efficiency.
 
• **Hyper-threading:** A technology used in some processors to enable a single core to handle multiple threads, though it does not replace the advantages of physical multi-core systems.
 
• **Single-core vs Multi-core:** Single-core processors execute one thread at a time, whereas multi-core processors can execute multiple threads or tasks concurrently.

• **Tab Management in Applications:**
 
 
• Tabbed interfaces are widely used in software applications to improve **workflow and organization**.
 
• Examples include web browsers, text editors, and spreadsheet programs.
 
• Switching between tabs using shortcuts saves time, especially for power users who work with multiple tabs simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Other Useful Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Alt + Tab**: Switches between open applications on Windows.
 
• **Cmd + Tab**: Switches between open applications on macOS.
 
• **Ctrl + F4**: Closes the current tab or window in applications.
 
 
 
• **Accessibility and Efficiency:**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are designed to make computing faster and more **accessible** for all users.
 
• They reduce reliance on the mouse, which can be especially helpful for individuals with repetitive strain injuries.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Find and Replace feature (Ctrl + H) in MS Word 2019?

options.text: To change the font of the selected text
To search for specific text and replace it with other text

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To search for specific text and replace it with other text**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Find and Replace** feature in MS Word 2019 is used to **locate specific text or phrases** within a document and replace them with alternative text if required.
 
• It is accessed using the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + H** or through the "Home" tab in the "Editing" group.
 
• This feature enables users to make **bulk changes** in a document efficiently, saving time and effort for repetitive edits.
 
• Advanced options in "Find and Replace" allow users to search for text with specific formatting, such as bold, italic, or specific fonts, and replace it with similar or modified formatting.
 
• It helps in maintaining consistency across large documents by ensuring uniform corrections or modifications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Search Options in Find and Replace:**

 
 
• Users can perform **case-sensitive searches** by enabling the "Match Case" option.
 
• The "Find Whole Words Only" option ensures only complete words matching the search term are located.
 
• Wildcard characters can be used to perform advanced and flexible searches.
 
 
 
• **Go To Feature:**
 
 
• The "Go To" tab within the Find and Replace dialog box allows users to navigate to specific pages, sections, or line numbers in a document.
 
 
 
• **Formatting Search:**
 
 
• Users can search for text with specific formatting attributes, such as font size, color, or paragraph settings, using the "Format" option in the dialog box.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• The feature does not support searching for non-text elements such as images or tables directly.
 
• Complex edits may require manual intervention despite using the Replace function.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Ideal for editing large documents, such as legal contracts, research papers, or reports, where repetitive terms or formatting need adjustment.

questions.question: When applying a watermark to an MS Word document, which of the following settings offers the LEAST control over its precise placement and size on each page?

options.text: Utilising a predefined watermark template from the 'Watermark' gallery
Inserting a custom picture watermark and adjusting its scale and wash-out settings
Inserting a graphic as a header or footer and positioning it behind the text
Inserting a custom text watermark with specific layout options

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Utilising a predefined watermark template from the 'Watermark' gallery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Predefined watermark templates in MS Word are designed for quick application but offer **limited customization** options for placement and size.
 
• These templates allow users to add watermarks like "Confidential," "Draft," or other predefined text, but the **precise positioning and scaling** are controlled automatically by MS Word.
 
• Unlike custom image or text watermarks, predefined templates restrict users from making **fine-tuned adjustments** to placement on the page.
 
• While predefined templates are convenient for general use, they lack the flexibility required to meet specific formatting or design requirements.
 
• Using other methods such as custom text, image watermarks, or graphic headers/footers provides **greater control** over design elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Watermarking in MS Word**

 
 
• A watermark is a text or image that appears behind the main document content.
 
• Commonly used for branding, document security, or indicating document status (e.g., "Draft").
 
• MS Word allows users to apply predefined or custom watermarks through the "Design" tab.
 
 
 
• **Custom Picture Watermark**
 
 
• Allows users to insert images as watermarks.
 
• Settings like "Scale" and "Washout" can be adjusted for better visual integration with the document.
 
• Provides flexibility in resizing and positioning the image.
 
 
 
• **Custom Text Watermark**
 
 
• Enables users to input specific text as the watermark.
 
• Offers options to adjust font, size, color, orientation, and placement.
 
• Highly customizable compared to predefined templates.
 
 
 
• **Using Graphics in Headers/Footers**
 
 
• Inserting graphics into headers or footers allows users to create custom watermarks.
 
• Provides full control over image placement, layering, and size.
 
• Graphics can be positioned behind text for a subtle watermark effect.
